ubo_and_aml_profiling.pep_and_sanctions_screening_protocols: Mandatory screening of all UBOs, directors, officers and authorized signatories against: (i) OFAC Specially Designated Nationals and Blocked Persons List and other OFAC sanctions lists; (ii) UN Security Council Consolidated List; (iii) the Canadian Sanctions List and Canadian Consolidated Autonomous Sanctions List maintained under the Special Economic Measures Act and United Nations Act; (iv) the United Kingdom and EU consolidated sanctions lists where relevant; and (v) FINTRAC politically exposed person (PEP) categories covering domestic and foreign PEPs, heads of international organizations, and their family members and close associates. Enhanced due diligence, senior management pre-approval, source of funds, and source of wealth verification are required for any PEP screening hit. Ongoing transaction monitoring applies to all direct and indirect UBOs holding 25% or more of voting rights or value.

statutory_name_clearance_protocol.registry_portal_name: Registraire des entreprises du Québec (Quebec Enterprise Registrar) — online name reservation and search module at www.registraireentreprises.gouv.qc.ca
statutory_name_clearance_protocol.language_and_transliteration_doctrine: French is the official language of Quebec under the Charter of the French Language, CQLR c C-11. A corporate name registered in Quebec must have an acceptable French version; non-French names must be transliterated into Latin characters and any foreign-language name must be accompanied by a clearly predominant French version. French-language documents are required for all entity filing purposes, and English or other-language documents must be accompanied by certified French translations. Legal elements such as 'Inc.', 'Corp.', 'Ltée' or 'Société par actions' are permitted.
statutory_name_clearance_protocol.extension_and_rejection_appeal_sop: If the proposed corporate name is rejected, the applicant has 30 days from the date of written refusal to file a formal request for reconsideration with the Registraire des entreprises du Québec under the Act respecting the legal publicity of enterprises and the Act respecting administrative justice, CQLR c J-3. The reconsideration request must include a revised French name, updated name-search evidence, a statutory declaration explaining the requested name, and any ministerial or professional authorizations required for sensitive tokens. If the Registrar affirms the refusal, the applicant may apply for judicial review before the Superior Court of Quebec under the Code of Civil Procedure within 30 days of the final decision; a further appeal lies to the Court of Appeal of Quebec only upon leave. A rejected name cannot be reserved for the same applicant while the reconsideration is pending.

registered_office_and_commercial_substan.virtual_office_permissibility: A Quebec Business Corporations Act corporation must maintain a registered office at a physical location in Quebec named in its articles. A virtual office or serviced office is acceptable for registry and service-of-process purposes if a real street address in Quebec and a responsible local corporate agent are in place, but a post-office box alone is not permitted. For ISIC 6201 personal wealth analytics and investment tracking software, no statutory physical branch is required. However, Canadian corporate-residence doctrine requires that central management and control (CEMC), including board decision-making, key contract execution, and actual management functions, remain in Canada; a mailbox-only virtual office without substantive management infrastructure creates elevated CRA residence recharacterization and General Anti-Avoidance Rule (GAAR) risk. To maintain commercial substance, local resident directors, Quebec-based board minutes, a local service contract, and an active registered-office address should be documented.
registered_office_and_commercial_substan.physical_inspection_likelihood: Low unanticipated physical-inspection risk: approximately 5–10% cumulative probability over the first three years for a low-risk software application company that does not handle client funds and uses third-party payment processors such as Stripe and Apple IAP. The likelihood rises to 15–25% if CRA, Revenu Québec or FINTRAC commences an audit, financial-statement anomalies are identified, or late or inconsistent UBO disclosures occur. Physical inspections are not routine for non-regulated fintech app developers and would generally be announced unless an audit or criminal-investigation threshold is met.

national_tax_registration_infrastructure.competent_tax_authority: Canada Revenue Agency (CRA) and Revenu Québec (RQ). Federal corporate income tax, GST/HST, and income tax administered by CRA; Quebec provincial corporate income tax and QST administered by Revenu Québec. Portals: CRA My Business Account and Revenu Québec's CLIC.
national_tax_registration_infrastructure.tax_id_procurement_sop: For a foreign entity establishing a Canadian business corporation in Quebec, the standard sequence is: (1) Incorporate under the Canada Business Corporations Act or the Quebec Business Corporations Act through Corporations Canada or Registraire des entreprises Québec, obtaining a Quebec Enterprise Number (NEQ) and, if federal, a corporate identification number. (2) After incorporation, register with CRA for a 9-digit Business Number (BN) using the Business Registration Online (BRO) service or by submitting RC1 form; add program accounts RT (corporate income tax) and RC (GST/HST). (3) Register with Revenu Québec for provincial corporate tax and QST, either through the BRO service or Registraire des entreprises, obtaining a Numéro d'inscription au fichier (NIF) and separate QST account. (4) Commence GST/HST and QST registration once taxable worldwide revenue exceeds CAD 30,000 or immediately for voluntary registration, and provide proof of non-resident ownership and provincial place of business for the Quebec business number.
national_tax_registration_infrastructure.statutory_election_mechanisms: Not applicable. Canada does not have a check-the-box regime. A Canadian corporation is taxed at the entity level under the Income Tax Act and cannot elect pass-through taxation. Hybrid mismatch rules under sections 18.4 to 18.6 and related provisions do not provide elective classification; they impose adjustments on certain hybrid arrangements. Elections limited to internal Canadian tax mechanisms such as section 216(4) elections for non-resident investment income and joint elections for Canadian-controlled private corporation business income allocation within a group.

indirect_taxation_nexus_and_rules.indirect_tax_system_name: GST/HST (Value-Added Tax) and Quebec Sales Tax (QST)
indirect_taxation_nexus_and_rules.statutory_registration_threshold_local_c: CAD 30,000 in worldwide annual taxable supplies for both GST/HST and QST small-supplier thresholds; once exceeded, mandatory registration. Financial portfolio tracking services are subject to this threshold unless zero-rated as exports.
indirect_taxation_nexus_and_rules.electronic_invoicing_and_clearance_manda: No federal or Quebec statutory mandate for real-time continuous control, digital stamping, or government pre-clearance of invoices. Suppliers must retain auditable electronic or paper invoices containing required statutory particulars. Quebec requires certain listed registrants to transmit prescribed data to Revenu Québec for exchange-of-information purposes, but no universal e-invoicing clearance API is enforced. Stripe and Apple IAP receipts do not replace statutory invoices; the selling entity must generate tax-compliant invoices for Canadian VAT/GST registrations, including supplier BN/QST registration number, date, description, GST/HST and QST charged, and terms. Real-time reporting is expected to modernize but is not yet legislated.

export_zero_rating_and_refund_substantia.zero_rating_eligibility: A Canadian registered supplier is eligible for 0% GST/HST and QST on exported goods and on certain services supplied to non-residents. For the fintech software/portfolio tracking service, zero-rating requires: (a) the recipient is a non-resident who is not registered for GST/HST and QST in the ordinary course of business in Canada; (b) the service is not, and is not performed on, real or tangible personal property situated in Canada; (c) the service is not a taxable Canadian 'financial service' supplied in Canada to a resident; and (d) evidence that the recipient is non-resident and the service is exported, such as the non-resident's business address and foreign payment method. The fact that payment flows through Stripe or Apple IAP does not in itself determine zero-rating; the 0% rate applies only if the statutory conditions are satisfied and documented. Domestic sales to Canadian residents and sales through a Canadian distribution platform may be taxable at 5% GST and 9.975% QST.
mandatory_customs_documentation_bundle: Canada Customs Export Declaration (B13A or Canada Border Services Agency 'Export Report') containing HS classification and value, where goods are physically exported
Signed commercial invoice identifying seller, buyer, export date, service or goods description, and foreign currency amount
Contract or service agreement showing the non-resident recipient and the place of supply outside Canada
Bill of Lading / Airway Bill / electronic carrier tracking record for tangible exports, or a service completion/usage record for intangible digital services
Foreign exchange settlement evidence from Stripe/Apple IAP or banking records confirming payment received from abroad
Where applicable, a Currency Exchange Memo or bank inward remittance statement (not a formal 'Inward Remittance Certificate' under Canadian law, but commonly used for audit substantiation)
export_zero_rating_and_refund_substantia.audit_scrutiny_and_clawback_penalties: CRA and Revenu Québec may reassess and claw back zero-rating claims together with interest and penalties where supporting documents are incomplete, false, or the supplier fails to demonstrate that the supply was exported or delivered outside Canada. Under the Excise Tax Act, sections 285 and 280 impose penalties up to 25% of any net tax understated for knowingly or under circumstances of gross negligence making false statements or omissions; section 281 imposes additional administrative penalties. Revenu Québec applies equivalent penalties under the Tax Administration Act. The limitation period for reassessment is normally four years from the date of the original assessment, but is extended to seven years where misrepresentation or fraud is proven. The exporter must retain the documentation bundle, including FX repatriation records, for at least six years from the end of the taxation year. Failure to repatriate foreign funds within a commercially reasonable period, and particularly beyond 180 days without documented justification, may trigger a factual inquiry into whether the transaction was a true export or a sham, leading to denial of zero-rating, re-characterization of the sale as a domestic taxable supply, assessment of GST/QST, interest, penalties, and, in egregious cases, criminal prosecution.

fx_control_regime_and_central_bank_regul.central_bank_authority: Bank of Canada (Banque du Canada) - Canada's central bank and monetary authority. No dedicated foreign-exchange administration exists; exchange-control policy is overseen by the Department of Finance Canada, prudential regulation of deposit-taking institutions by the Office of the Superintendent of Financial Institutions (OSFI), AML/ATF supervision by the Financial Transactions and Reports Analysis Centre of Canada (FINTRAC), and Quebec financial-market conduct by the Autorité des marchés financiers (AMF).
fx_control_regime_and_central_bank_regul.currency_convertibility_assessment: Canada maintains a freely floating currency with no exchange-control approval regime and no substantive distinction between capital-account and current-account convertibility. Equity injections, loan repayments, dividends, interest, royalties and service fees are fully convertible and remittable in CAD. Profit-remittance hurdles are tax-only: Part XIII federal withholding tax at 25% (treaty-reduced to 15% for portfolio dividends and 5% for a US corporate beneficial owner holding at least 10% of voting shares) plus the parallel Quebec dividend withholding administered by Revenu Québec; no central-bank permit, waiting period, proportionality test or conversion tax applies. Corporations may freely hold USD/EUR balances in domestic foreign-currency accounts.
fx_control_regime_and_central_bank_regul.export_proceeds_surrender_rules: None. Canada imposes no statutory surrender obligation, repatriation timeline, or mandatory conversion ratio on export or SaaS/service receipts. Invoice proceeds may be retained in foreign-currency accounts at Canadian or offshore banks. The only applicable duty is FINTRAC's automatic reporting of international electronic funds transfers (EFTs) of CAD 10,000 or more, which is filed by the clearing financial institution and does not require the operating corporation to repatriate or convert funds.

tier1_domestic_commercial_banks.bank_name: National Bank of Canada (Banque Nationale du Canada)

tier1_domestic_commercial_banks.account_class: Operational Account and USD international clearing

corporate_banking_onboarding_blueprint.fintech_emi_cross_border_viability: Medium - ancillary use only. Canada has no Electronic Money Institution (EMI) licensing category; offshore digital finance platforms (Wise, Revolut Business, Airwallex, Currenxie, Mercury) cannot lawfully hold Canadian statutory capital or serve as the primary bank relationship because they are not authorized deposit-taking institutions under the Bank Act. They may be engaged as payment facilitators for cross-border receivables and vendor payouts through partnered Canadian money-services-business (MSB) arrangements, but the principal account, capital escrow and audit trail must sit with a regulated Schedule I Canadian bank.
corporate_banking_onboarding_blueprint.physical_presence_and_kyc_interview_mand: Remote opening is generally permitted for a low-risk Canadian software corporation. The Proceeds of Crime (Money Laundering) and Terrorist Financing Act (PCMLTFA) does not mandate branch attendance; banks accept video-interview KYC, eSignature and digital identity verification (Experian, Equifax, SecureKey). Physical presence becomes de facto required only when beneficial owners are non-resident, the corporate structure is complex, or the UBO resides in a high-risk jurisdiction. At least one director or authorized signatory must hold a verifiable Canadian address; non-resident directors must supply certified passport copies, proof of residential address issued within the last six months, and a professional or banking reference, and may be asked to complete a notarized signature card at a Canadian consulate.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: Product branding ('Personal Wealth Analytics and Investment Tracking') raises suspicion of unregistered securities dealing or portfolio-management activity under Quebec securities law.
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: Quebec-counsel legal opinion confirming the application is a data-analytics and tracking software under ISIC 6201; product technical documentation showing no order execution or client-fund custody; SaaS terms of service and privacy policy; confirmation that Stripe and Apple IAP are the only payment rails; AMF registration exemption analysis.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: Perceived Money Services Business (MSB) activity because the corporation collects subscription fees through payment aggregators and may route cross-border funds.
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: Signed FINTRAC MSB self-assessment confirming the entity is not an MSB under the PCMLTFA; executed PSP agreements with Stripe and Apple demonstrating that payment processing, clearing and settlement are performed by licensed third parties; corporate policy prohibiting cash, cheque-cashing, money transmission or acting as an intermediary; revenue-flow diagram.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: Non-resident beneficial owners or a cross-border holding structure without sufficient economic substance in Quebec.
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: Registraire des entreprises certificate of status; articles of incorporation; registered-office lease; payroll and contractor records; board resolutions; UBO declarations with certified passports and proof of address; source-of-wealth and source-of-funds statements; banking references from the UBOs' existing institutions.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: Initial capital injection received by a single large wire from a foreign jurisdiction without documented share issuance.
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: Share subscription agreement and share-certificate records; board resolution authorizing issuance; provenance letter from the remitting shareholder's bank; updated capital-stock ledger; tax clearance or filing confirmation where applicable; bank-account statement trace.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: High anticipated disbursement velocity to overseas cloud providers and contractors, raising round-tripping or money-laundering concerns.
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: Executed vendor and subcontractor contracts; invoices and delivery/service-acceptance records; twelve-month cash-flow forecast; treasury policy restricting payments to named beneficiaries; commitment to monthly reconciliation and audit-trail reporting.

cross_border_liquidity_and_clearing_rail.inbound_capital_injection_routing: Execute the share issuance first (subscription agreement, board resolution, updated share register), then have the non-resident shareholder remit by SWIFT MT103 to the corporation's designated CAD operational account at a Schedule I Quebec bank, with the purpose text 'equity contribution - subscription for common shares'. No Investment Canada Act filing or exchange-control clearance is required for a software business under the WTO investor thresholds. FINTRAC receives the bank's EFT report automatically for wires of CAD 10,000 or more; no separate corporate filing is needed. Foreign-currency capital may be converted at the bank's commercial rate or held in a parallel USD account. To avoid 'back-to-back' or third-party-funding flags, the first wire must originate from the UBO's own name-matched account, not from an unrelated entity.
cross_border_liquidity_and_clearing_rail.outbound_trade_disbursements: Cross-border vendor, cloud and licensing payments should be settled by SWIFT MT103 customer credit transfer (MT202 for bank-to-bank cover). Domestic CAD disbursements use Interac e-Transfer (sub-CAD 10,000), online wire/EFT, or ACSS batch ACH for payroll and recurring fees. High-value procurement requiring payment assurance may use commercial letters of credit under UCP600 issued by the Montreal trade desks of National Bank, RBC or BMO; documentary collections (CAD/DRAFT) are a secondary instrument. All cross-border instructions above CAD 10,000 are automatically reported by the bank under FINTRAC EFT rules. Disbursements to non-resident related parties must be supported by transfer-pricing documentation (T106/T1134 as applicable) and arm's-length invoices to preserve tax deductions.
permissible_fx_hedging_instruments: Deliverable FX forward contracts (CAD/USD, CAD/EUR) with 1-12 month tenors
FX swaps (spot-forward combinations) for short-term liquidity conversion
Cross-currency interest rate swaps (CCS/CRS) under ISDA/CSA Master Agreements
Vanilla OTC FX put and call options with premium paid in CAD
Non-deliverable forwards (NDFs) for restricted-currency settlements (not required for CAD/USD flows)
Spot contracts with T+0/T+1 settlement for conversion of receipts and dividend/royalty payments

annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deliverable: Federal Annual Return (Canada Business Corporations Act, s. 263)
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.receiving_authority: Corporations Canada (Innovation, Science and Economic Development Canada)
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deadline_window: Within 60 days after the anniversary date of federal incorporation each year (e.g., incorporation on 15 March -> filing due by 14 May).
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.delinquency_sanctions: No monetary late penalty; failure to file for two consecutive years permits the Director under CBCA s. 240(4) to commence administrative dissolution after a 120-day notice. Non-compliance also delays issuance of certificate of compliance and may affect bank / payment-rail (Stripe, Apple IAP) verification.

annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deliverable: Quebec Annual Declaration (Déclaration annuelle) under the Act respecting the legal publicity of enterprises (CQLR c P-44.1)
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deadline_window: Within 60 days following the anniversary date of the enterprise's registration in the REQ registry (anniversary date of the company's immatriculation).
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.delinquency_sanctions: REQ publishes a default notice and imposes a late fee; failure to file for two consecutive years leads to administrative strike-off (radiation) and, under the Quebec Business Corporations Act, potential dissolution by the registraire; struck-off corporations lose legal personality and directors may face personal liability for certain corporate debts.

corporate_income_tax_regime.statutory_headline_rate: 26.5% combined general corporate rate (federal 15% plus Quebec 11.5%); 12.2% combined effective rate for a Canadian-controlled private corporation (CCPC) on the first CAD 500,000 of active business income (federal small business deduction 9% plus Quebec small business deduction 3.2%).
corporate_income_tax_regime.effective_tax_rate_incentives: SR&ED investment tax credits: federal 15% non-refundable (35% refundable for CCPCs on up to CAD 3,000,000 qualifying expenditures) plus Quebec refundable SR&ED credits at 14%–30%; no IP patent-box enacted; general rate reduction yields 15% federal headline; CCPC small business deduction lowers effective rate to 12.2% on first CAD 500,000.
